images.filename: Eileen Chamberlain Donahoe, Andrej Logar and Jerry Matjila.jpg
images.caption:
Ambassador Eileen Chamberlain Donahoe, U.S. Representative to the Human Rights Council, with Ambassador Andrej Logar, Permanent Representative of Slovenia, Vice President of the Human Rights Council, and Ambassador Jerry Matjila, Permanent Representative of South Africa to the United Nations in Geneva, on World Cup Kickoff Day.
The Permanent Mission of South Africa has invited diplomats from qualifying countries to wear their national jerseys to the United Nations on Fridays during the duration of the World Cup.

U.S. Mission Photo: Eric Bridiers
images.alt:
Ambassador Eileen Chamberlain Donahoe, U.S. Representative to the Human Rights Council, with Ambassador Andrej Logar, Permanent Representative of Slovenia, Vice President of the Human Rights Council, and Ambassador Jerry Matjila, Permanent Representative of South Africa to the United Nations in Geneva, on World Cup Kickoff Day.
The Permanent Mission of South Africa has invited diplomats from qualifying countries to wear their national jerseys to the United Nations on Fridays during the duration of the World Cup.

U.S. Mission Photo: Eric Bridiers

images.filename: U-11 Bafokeng Football Academy Teams Preview 2010 World Cup Match Between U.S. and Ghana.jpg
images.caption: Two Under-11 Bafokeng Football Academy teams preview the FIFA 2010 World Cup match between the United States and Ghana by playing each other as the “U.S.” and Ghana” on June 25, 2010, in Rustenburg, South Africa. The game highlighted the development of rural soccer in South Africa, particularly in the Royal Bafokeng Nation, which consists of twenty-nine villages located in the Rustenburg Valley in the North West Province. [State Department photo/ Public Domain]
images.alt: Two Under-11 Bafokeng Football Academy teams preview the FIFA 2010 World Cup match between the United States and Ghana by playing each other as the “U.S.” and Ghana” on June 25, 2010, in Rustenburg, South Africa. The game highlighted the development of rural soccer in South Africa, particularly in the Royal Bafokeng Nation, which consists of twenty-nine villages located in the Rustenburg Valley in the North West Province. [State Department photo/ Public Domain]
